source.document: WHO SMART Guidelines — Antenatal Care (DAK L2)

declencheur: ANC.B10. Counselling, in-facility management and treatment
regle_metier: IF the woman is currently in a malaria-endemic setting, or in an area where there is greater than 20% prevalence of infection with any soil-transmitted helminths, THEN she should receive preventative treatment accordingly

regles.annotation: Sleeping under an insecticide-treated bednet and the importance of seeking care and getting treatment as soon as she has any symptoms
regles.reference: WHO ANC recommendations (2016): C.6. Malaria prevention: intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy (IPTp) (3)

regles.sortie: "IPTp-SP dose 1 provided" = FALSE "IPTp-SP dose 2 provided" = FALSE "IPTp-SP dose 3 provided" = FALSE
regles.action: Do not give IPTp-SP, because woman is taking co-trimoxazole
regles.annotation: IF the woman is currently taking co-trimoxazole, even in a malaria-endemic setting, she should not receive any dose of IPTp-SP. Women who are taking co-trimoxazole SHOULD NOT receive IPTp-SP. Taking both co-trimoxazole and IPTp-SP together can enhance side-effects, especially haematological side-effects such as anaemia.
regles.reference: WHO ANC recommendations (2016): C.6. Malaria prevention: intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy (IPTp) (3)

regles.annotation: In areas with a population prevalence of infection with any soil-transmitted helminths of 20% or higher OR a population anaemia prevalence 40% or higher, preventive anthelminthic treatment is recommended for pregnant women after the first trimester as part of worm infection reduction programmes
regles.reference: WHO ANC recommendations (2016): C.4. Preventive anthelminthic treatment (3)
